anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level statements or transaction design force the engine to scan, join, or return far more data than business logic requires.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : The database process allocates buffer cache, work memory, plan cache, and other heaps beyond the safe physical memory envelope, provoking OS-level pressure.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Physical or logical free space in data files, logs, or temporary areas drops to a hard boundary, risking allocation failures and stalled writes.

When all three root causes manifest together, the database experiences a compound failure mode: chatty or over-broad SQL rapidly fills buffer caches and per-query work areas, driving resident-set size to the limit. As memory pressure mounts, the engine begins spilling sort, hash, and intermediate result sets to temporary segments, which in turn accelerates consumption of data-file, temp, and log space. The already space-starved storage layer struggles to extend or recycle files, causing write stalls, "out of space" errors, aborted transactions, and repeated retries from the application layer. Performance telemetry shows a mix of long-tail statement latency, swapping or OOM events, and sudden allocation failures in temporary or archive areas—symptoms that, when observed in isolation, are difficult to attribute to any single layer.

Causal chain: overly expensive SQL (1) inflates memory demand, inflating caches and per-operation work buffers; (2) this pushes the instance into heavy paging or triggers aggressive spill-to-disk behavior; (3) the resulting temporary and log growth rapidly depletes remaining storage capacity; (4) once space is exhausted, memory-relief spills fail, forcing even more memory retention and amplifying OOM risk. Each anomaly therefore feeds the next: inefficient workload begets memory saturation, memory saturation begets disk spills, and disk spills exhaust space, which in turn prevents the memory layer from offloading work, creating a feedback loop that can cascade into node eviction, service outage, or data-load failure.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle within an open transaction for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle, waiting for a client query, while an open transaction remains active longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; this prevents long idle transactions from holding locks or preventing vacuum cleanup.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
